Liam: Quick sync — FinCo (enterprise) is asking for p99 <= 450ms for 512-token gen at ~200 qps per region. They want this in contract. Is that doable with current kernels/batching?
Ava: Clarifying — is that end-to-end gen including network + serialization? Are they ok with a p95 carve-out or warmup window?
Liam: Yes E2E. They expect production routing + auth. Will accept a warmup clause but want steady-state guarantees after 10m.
Rohit: Short answer: not without tradeoffs. With our current kernel selection + microbatch settings we hit ~p95 220ms, p99 ~620ms at 200 qps for 512 toks on A100-80GB perf profile.
Jia: From profiling yesterday: KV cache cold miss penalty is ~80-120ms for some long histories. Kernel switch overhead (fp16->int8 path) adds ~30-50ms on first token if we swap.
Marta: So KV warmup is the main tail source? Can Sales negotiate a carveout for first 5-10k requests after deployment? :thinking: 
Rohit: The tail is multi-factor: microbatch tailing, KV cold misses, and occasional kernel scheduling jitter under high concurrency. Microbatch=1 minimizes latency but reduces throughput by ~30%. Microbatch=4 hits target throughput but p99 tails worsen.
Ava: What do the perf regressions look like — anything recent that pushed p99 up?
Jia: We observed a regression tied to the scheduler change in commit c3a9bf — that introduced a high-variance queuing policy. Reverted in staging improved p99 by ~120ms. Bug: PERF-3242.
CI-bot: Perf job 2026-07-11T14:02:05Z: baseline vs head: p95 +5ms, p99 +110ms on 512-token perf benchmark — link: https://ci.internal/runs/1422
Rohit: Mitigations we can offer: 1) enforce a small pre-warm stream for customer traffic to populate KV (adds ops but helps tails), 2) set microbatch cap to 2 with dynamic smaller batch scoring for latency-sensitive routes, 3) pin kernel to low-latency variant (cost up slightly), 4) server-side prompt length enforcement/ truncation.
Jia: Also suggest progressive rollout: canary at 20% with KV priming, monitor tail/quality for 48h. We can add automatic fallback to a slightly larger model variant if tail spikes.
Liam: Customer will push back on cost increases. They need contractual p99 450ms or we lose them. Can we offer a SLA with an exception for initial warmup + a higher-cost 'latency premium' tier?
Ava: Proposal for contract language: p95 250ms guaranteed steady-state; p99 contractual target 450ms with carveouts: (a) first 30m after deploy, (b) requests with effective context length > 2x baseline, (c) scheduled maintenance windows. Also offer a premium latency tier (extra fee) that pins low-latency kernels + dedicated microbatch config.
Rohit: Implementation checklist if Sales accepts: - PERF-3242 rollback in prod or safer scheduler - Add KV prewarm hook for customer on attach - Route config: latency-tier route that sets microbatch_max=2 and kernel_variant=low_latency - End-to-end perf smoke tests + SL annotated logs
Marta: Sounds good. Sales will push the premium tier. Need a conservative SLO we can commit to now. Recommend: p95 250ms, p99 600ms contractual without premium; p99 450ms with premium + warmup.
Liam: I can take that to FinCo. Can eng produce a one-pager with numbers and mitigations? They want numbers for cost delta too.
Rohit: I'll assemble perf numbers + cost estimate (GPU-hours delta, kernel cost proxy) by EOD tomorrow. Will include microbatch throughput curves and p95/p99 vs qps.
Jia: I'll attach profiling snippets and the KV cold-warm graphs to the one-pager. Also include recommended priming script: ```bash
# priming script example
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"input":"prewarm prompt"}' >/dev/null
done
```
Ava: Product will draft contract language and the warmup SLA clause.
CI-bot: Deploy job queued for scheduler rollback candidate #perf-3242-rollback at 2026-07-12T02:00:00Z
Marta: Thanks all. Liam, loop me into any customer calls. Rohit/Jia, drop your slides/one-pager in #eng-runtime when ready. :thumbsup:
Rohit: Will do. Filing PERF-3242 followups: PERF-3242-1 (rollback review), PERF-3242-2 (long-term scheduler fix).
Liam: Meeting with FinCo scheduled Fri 10:00 PT. I'll propose the two-tier approach.
Ava: Agree. If this starts getting too bespoke, we should push toward productized 'latency premium' offering.
Marta: Noted. Closing notes: owner assignments -> Liam (customer), Rohit (perf numbers + changes), Jia (profiling + scripts), Ava (contract language). Last quick flag: we may need SRE involvement for dedicated routing — @Oncall when we have the rollout window.
Rohit: tagging SRE in the ticket. End of thread.
